# Final Revision Sheet

*Generated by `python scripts/build_viva.py` from the project's own
outputs. Every figure below is read from `outputs/tables/report_facts.json`,
the same fact pack used by the report and the presentation. The dataset is
synthetic and is described as such throughout.*

Read this on the way to the viva.

## Project in 5 lines

1. A customer revenue intelligence platform: transactions in, business
   decisions out.
2. Synthetic retail dataset, 18,670 validated order lines,
   1,984 customers, 36 months, ₹6.01 Cr delivered
   revenue.
3. Two independent segmentations, customer value, next-quarter prediction and a
   six-month forecast — all on one validated dataset and one revenue
   definition.
4. Delivered through 57 reconciled SQL queries, a Power BI
   model of 84 DAX measures, and a 12-page
   Streamlit application.
5. Integration tested, not asserted: 135 automated checks,
   134 pass, 0 fail.

## Dataset in 5 lines

1. Synthetic, generated from seed 42; describes no real business.
2. 18,819 raw order lines → 18,670 clean;
   149 duplicates removed.
3. 2,000 registered customers, 1,984 purchasing;
   61 products, 6 categories.
4. 35 cities, 21 states, 5 regions;
   01 January 2023 to 31 December 2025.
5. Revenue counts **delivered lines only**; ₹62.55 L
   (9.43%) of booked value lost to returns and cancellations.

## Methodology in 5 lines

1. Rule-driven cleaning with an audit trail: 941 rows failed a
   rule before treatment, zero after.
2. 28 engineered columns —
   calendar, delivered flag, revenue/profit/margin, bands, outlier flags,
   arithmetic reconciliation.
3. EDA across time, product, geography, discount, payment and customer.
4. Three validation gates: business rules, K-selection, forecast baseline.
5. Every stage a separate module with one entry point, reading only the
   persisted output of the stage before it.

## ML in 5 lines

1. RFM: quintile scores at 2026-01-01, 11 rule-based
   segments over 1,984 customers.
2. K-Means on the same three features after log1p -> StandardScaler (sklearn Pipeline saved in rfm_scaler.pkl).
3. K = 4 by three pre-declared rules, then highest silhouette:
   0.3534.
4. Clusters: 0 High-Value, Active 364, 1 Low-Value, Active 453, 2 Mid-Value, Lapsing 753, 3 Low-Value, Inactive 414.
5. Agreement with RFM: ARI 0.3952 — same high-value group, divergence
   in the middle.

## Prediction in 5 lines

1. Target: Next_Quarter_Revenue = Delivered Sales (Rs) in the 3 months after the cutoff.
2. Panel 10,393 customer-quarter rows, 24 features,
   all pre-cutoff.
3. Chronological split 4,788 / 2,692 / 2,913;
   leakage audit found none.
4. Linear regression selected by rule: simplest model within 2% of the best validation RMSE (fixed in advance).
5. Test MAE ₹5,658, R² 0.0557, bias 1.12% — weak per
   customer, usable at portfolio level, because 53.0% of
   customer-quarters are zero.

## Forecasting in 5 lines

1. Company monthly delivered revenue, 36 months.
2. ADF p = 0.2015 — non-stationary in level.
3. Naive, seasonal naive, ETS, ARIMA/SARIMA and Theta tested; Theta: Theta (seasonality auto-tested)
   selected.
4. Test MAE ₹213,179, test MAPE 7.77%, **backtest mean
   MAPE 14.56%** over 7 folds — quote the backtest.
5. 6 months (2026-01 to 2026-06): ₹1.58 Cr, 80% interval
   ₹1.00 Cr–₹2.16 Cr, against ₹1.50 Cr in the previous six
   months.

## Dashboard in 5 lines

1. SQL: 11 tables, 2 views,
   57 queries, all 56 checks pass.
2. Power BI: star schema, 13 tables, 9
   relationships, 84 DAX measures in 10
   folders.
3. 48/48 measures validated against SQL;
   32 consistency checks pass.
4. Power BI Desktop unavailable (Windows-only) — the nine pages are labelled

5. Streamlit: 12 pages, loads persisted models, computes no metric

## Key findings

- Top 10% of customers = 45.39% of revenue; top 20% = 64.33%.
- Champions: 16.84% of customers, 53.83% of
  revenue.
- Two independent methods find the same high-value group (ARI
  0.3952).
- 52 high-value customers inactive 180+ days, holding
  ₹26.51 L.
- Repeat customers: 89.42% of the base,
  98.59% of revenue (₹33,378 vs
  ₹4,019 each).
- Electronics leads volume (50.10%) at the lowest margin
  (10.85%); Beauty earns 46.49%.
- Zero-discount band is best-margin in 6 of
  6 categories — association, not cause.
- Growth is not bought with margin: 51.4% then
  37.7%, margin rising to 23.90%.
- No regional margin problem: 0 of 30 pairs
  below national.
- Company forecasting works (14.56%); individual prediction does not
  (0.0557).

## Limitations

Synthetic data · 36-month history · weak individual prediction ·
univariate forecast · association not causation · no churn label in the data ·
Power BI pages are mockups · no user testing · no deployment or monitoring.

## Future scope

Real data under a data-protection agreement · a business-defined inactivity
label and a supervised model for it · two-stage prediction (will they order,
then how much) · external regressors in the forecast · a controlled discount
experiment · scheduled re-runs with drift monitoring · complete the Power BI
build on Windows.

## If you are stuck

- **A number you cannot recall:** "That value was not something I memorised —
  it is in the report; what I can tell you is the direction and why."
- **A technique you did not use:** "It was considered as a possible extension,
  but it was not part of the implemented pipeline."
- **A result the project does not contain:** "That value was not directly
  measured in this project."

Never invent a number. An honest gap costs one mark; a fabricated figure that
is checked costs the viva.
